A free browser game is going viral for letting players spend as much time as they want petting adorable cats, complete with different fur patterns, customizable sizes, and relaxing purring sounds.

Created by Japanese developer zubu, Cat Petting Simulator was released on November 22, 2026, and has swiftly become a hit among cat lovers.

Industry observers note that the concept couldn’t be simpler. Rather than completing challenges or earning points, players are presented with a cat lounging on a couch, and their only objective is to pet it.

Using a mouse or touchscreen, players can stroke the feline’s back, watching as its fur and body react to their movements.

According to Famitsu, the game offers 13 different cat appearances, including black cats, white cats, orange tabbies, and Siamese cats.

Players can also adjust their cat’s size and body width, allowing them to create everything from a small kitten to a particularly chunky feline.

It has been revealed that the attention to detail is surprisingly impressive. As players move their hands across the cat, its fur shifts realistically while its body squishes and stretches in response.

There’s even an option to enable purring sounds, while a nighttime mode changes the room’s lighting for a more relaxing atmosphere.

In a recent development, the game has already attracted considerable attention online. As Automaton reported, players have praised the realistic petting animations, with some joking that it’s their game of the year despite launching days after GTA 6.

The developer’s original announcement also surpassed 120,000 likes on X within a day of release.

This isn’t the first unusual cat-themed browser game to attract attention in 2026. Back in April, a viral game challenged players to brush an orange cat without getting bitten.

Cat Petting Simulator is completely free to play on its official website, with no download required on PC or mobile.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A “Chinese spy” lookalike contest took over New York City’s Washington Square Park, with participants performing mock espionage acts for a cash prize.
  • The competition took place on November 21 and was organized by FactMachine and Prez, drawing a crowd of spectators who were given the opportunity to vote for their favorite contestants.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A “Chinese spy” lookalike contest took over New York City’s Washington Square Park, with participants performing mock espionage acts for a cash prize.

The competition took place on November 21 and was organized by FactMachine and Prez, drawing a crowd of spectators who were given the opportunity to vote for their favorite contestants.

The event was inspired by the ongoing controversy surrounding Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, who had resigned as CEO just over a week before the competition took place.

Around 10 women participated in the competition, dressing up as spies and performing various espionage-inspired acts in front of the crowd.

Some contestants pretended to pull classified documents from their pockets, while another person dressed up as Jensen Huang joined in with the performances.

Spectators were able to decide the winner by scanning QR codes displayed at the venue and voting for their favorite participant, with a $50 cash prize up for grabs.

A post shared by Keri | NYC Content Creator (@keri_nyc).

The contest came after Nvidia launched an independent investigation on November 8 into reports that its CEO had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. Huang also admitted to being unfaithful to his wife in a message sent to employees.

On November 12, he resigned as president, CEO, and a member of Nvidia’s board of directors, ending his 33-year tenure leading the company. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO.

However, just two days after the lookalike contest, Nvidia revealed that Huang had been reinstated following a unanimous vote by its board of directors.

It has been revealed that the tech giant noted it had consulted senior US government officials and was confident that his return posed no national security risk. Its independent investigation remains ongoing, with Huang committing to cooperate.

Hila Klein has announced that she is stepping away from the H3 podcast amid her divorce from Ethan Klein, as he has been teasing a comeback.

Back on October 22, Ethan Klein confirmed that the H3 Podcast was going on an “indefinite hiatus,” before his wife, Hila Klein, revealed that he had been having an affair for over six months. Hila confirmed that she had filed for divorce from Ethan, adding: “I am living in a nightmare I can’t wake up from.”.

Ethan also revealed that he would be giving up any stake in the H3 podcast, as well as their other ventures, suggesting that the podcast crew would be making a return.

It has been revealed that “I’m so sorry to share that I’ve made the difficult decision to stop working on the new show. I truly tried with every ounce of strength I had to make this work, but after everything that has happened, I’ve come to realize that I can’t continue down this path while also giving myself the space I need to heal and protect my mental health,” she stated on November 23.

Hila added that she needs to “focus on myself, my healing, and what’s best for me and my kids,” before noting that she is “devastated” about ending the show.

“Walking away from something that has been such a huge part of my life is incredibly painful,” she continued. “I will miss you all more than I can put into words. Thank you for all the love and support over the years.”.

Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dexerto ↗ Open Full Page

Discord can now automatically save gaming clips when your friends start laughing

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (470 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dexerto

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Discord’s newly introduced Auto Clips automatically saves gameplay moments when it hears a voice chat erupt in laughter or shouting, and it’s rolling out to Nitro members now.
  • Whether you’re playing a chaotic game of Fortnite or getting your friends together for another significant Minecraft marathon, being able to instantly capture those moments that leave you in stitches of laughter is imperative.
  • After all, we’ve all been in situations where you’ve forgotten to hit record or your capture software has decided to stop working (it couldn’t be me).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Discord’s newly introduced Auto Clips automatically saves gameplay moments when it hears a voice chat erupt in laughter or shouting, and it’s rolling out to Nitro members now.

Whether you’re playing a chaotic game of Fortnite or getting your friends together for another significant Minecraft marathon, being able to instantly capture those moments that leave you in stitches of laughter is imperative.

After all, we’ve all been in situations where you’ve forgotten to hit record or your capture software has decided to stop working (it couldn’t be me). Enter Discord’s Auto Clips, a fresh feature that can detect when your group starts laughing or shouting before pulling together a clip of what just happened.

Unlike other capture software, Discord Auto Clips removes the need to hit a keyboard shortcut to record clips. Instead, it uses a small machine learning model that runs locally on the user’s PC, which continuously looks for audio cues resembling laughter or shouting, then uses those reactions to flag moments that might be worth saving.

Discord has revealed that the model cannot understand conversations or identify individual speakers, while any footage that is not saved as a clip is discarded after the gaming session ends.

Auto Clips can also work without voice chat in Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, League of Legends, and Rocket League. Discord uses integrations with those games to recognize events such as kills, goals, and completed rounds, with support for more titles planned in the future.

We've been cooking on Clips since Early Access debuted in 2023.Now there's 🢂Ａｕｔｏ Ｃｌｉｐｓ🢀When you and your friends break out laughing in voice, Discord saves the moment. No keybinds or additional setup needed. Starting today, Auto Clips is rolling out to Nitro… pic.twitter.com/a70itXDB1f.

Up to three highlights can be saved during each session, after which players can review them through Discord’s Clips library. It’s here that each recording can be trimmed, renamed, and edited with text or images, while game and voice audio can be removed before you share it with your friends or the wider internet.

Discord testing new “Game Mode” feature to help your PC run better.

Discord will soon let anyone find public server messages through Google.

Discord doubles Nitro upload limit to 1GB alongside server organization features.

Discord says clips remain stored locally on the player’s PC unless they choose to post them, and the company does not use saved footage, voice recordings, or other user data to train its detection model.

If you want to opt out of the feature, Discord states that consumers will be able to disable Auto Clips entirely or prevent their voice from appearing in clips recorded by other people. The feature began rolling out to Nitro members in Early Access on November 24 and is presently only available through Discord’s Windows desktop app.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that as artificial intelligence has become an everyday part of life for a lot of people, it has also helped travellers looking to plot out journeys.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An influencer using AI prompts to score cheap upgrades on flights has reportedly ended up overpaying compared to normal prices.

Recent findings suggest that as artificial intelligence has become an everyday part of life for a lot of people, it has also helped travellers looking to plot out journeys. Many have used ChatGPT to scout out restaurant, hotels, and even score deals on flights. Though, others have fallen foul of fake AI ads for travel hotspots that don’t actually exist.

However, as per travel experts at One Mile at a Time, an influencer who has been advertising a ChatGPT script to get cheaper upgrades on flights, seemingly ended up overpaying.

MavGPT laid out three prompts for ChatGPT, including urging the AI to ask about what airmiles you have, as well as checking if a flight you’re booked on has any upgrade available. In his example, he claimed he was flying with American Airlines Los Angeles to London Heathrow, with the AI spending 52,000 miles and a $190 fee for the upgrade.

According to One Mile at a Time, MavGPT “got screwed” if that was the AI’s best idea, seeing as it took the instant upgrade offer that the airline offer anyway.

They added that it wasn’t an “actual trick or hack,” and the AI should have looked at the “systemwide upgrade” seeing as there were still empty seats available.

“While there are definitely some strong use cases for AI, I think this is actually a pretty poor showing of what it can do,” they added, noting that the miles could have easily been saved and spent on “something else” instead.

Latest Update: Why you should upgrade to an OLED for GTA 6

💡 Key Takeaways
  • With GTA 6 bringing players back to Vice City, many are already thinking about how to get the most out of Rockstar’s next open-world game when it rolls out.
  • With neon-lit streets, crowded nightlife, tropical beaches and surrounding landscapes of Leonida, GTA 6 is Rockstar’s most visually ambitious release yet.
  • While much of the conversation is focused on how consoles will handle it, the display you use is likely to make a more noticeable difference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With GTA 6 bringing players back to Vice City, many are already thinking about how to get the most out of Rockstar’s next open-world game when it rolls out.

With neon-lit streets, crowded nightlife, tropical beaches and surrounding landscapes of Leonida, GTA 6 is Rockstar’s most visually ambitious release yet.

While much of the conversation is focused on how consoles will handle it, the display you use is likely to make a more noticeable difference.

OLED technology has become increasingly popular thanks to its deep blacks, strong contrast, and vibrant colors. For a game featuring the diverse environments shown in GTA 6’s trailers, and especially paired with HDR, those advantages make upgrading your display the obvious choice.

Sources indicate that unlike traditional LCD monitors, OLED displays can turn individual pixels off completely, producing those luxuriously deep blacks. That will make GTA 6’s neon-lit streets, nighttime environments, and colorful landscapes look far more impressive.

For GTA 6, those improvements will be particularly noticeable in several environments players have already seen in Rockstar’s trailers:.

Modern OLED gaming monitors have also introduced technologies designed to improve brightness and visibility across different environments.

GIGABYTE’s AORUS FO32U24G features a 32-inch 4K display built around a fourth-generation Tandem WOLED panel. Its RealBlack Glossy screen treatment is designed to preserve deep blacks and perceived contrast while reducing reflections.

Recent findings suggest that the monitor also features HyperNits, a technology that adjusts HDR brightness to help prevent images from appearing overly dark. According to GIGABYTE, HyperNits can increase overall brightness by up to 30% while preserving highlight details.

That will be particularly relevant to GTA 6’s varied environments, where players will frequently transition between bright sunlight, darker interiors, and nighttime scenes.

Although high-end gaming monitors are often associated with PC gaming, OLED’s picture quality advantages aren’t limited to players with expensive gaming computers.

GTA 6 is scheduled to launch on PS5, PS5 Pro, and Xbox Series X|S.

Both the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S support modern display features, including HDR and up to 120Hz output in compatible games.

For console players, there are three main display features worth considering:.

GIGABYTE’s FO32U24G and FO27Q28G both feature HDMI 2.1 connectivity, making them options for players who use their monitors with consoles as well as PCs.

And while consoles won’t maximise these monitors’ refresh rates of 240Hz and 280Hz, OLED’s visual improvements will be just as glorious.

Recent findings suggest that even at lower frame rates, OLED’s contrast, black levels, and color reproduction will improve how supported games look. Of course, GTA 6’s final rendering resolution and performance modes remain dependent on Rockstar’s implementation.

Despite the advantages of OLED, burn-in remains one of the most common concerns surrounding the technology.

Sources indicate that burn-in occurs when uneven pixel wear leaves persistent image retention on a display. This can become a consideration when static elements remain visible for extended periods, including health bars, mini-maps, and other interface elements commonly found in video games.

For a game like GTA 6, where players could spend hundreds of hours exploring the open world, long-term display protection is worth considering.

Sources indicate that GIGABYTE addresses this with AI OLED Care Pro, available on the AORUS FO32U24G and FO27Q28G. The system automatically manages brightness, performs pixel cleaning during idle periods, and powers down the display when users step away.

It also includes Cooling Force technology, which uses integrated heat pipes to help manage panel temperatures during extended use.

While OLED technology offers several advantages, choosing the right display involves more than simply deciding between OLED and LCD.

Screen size, resolution, panel technology, and room lighting can all influence which monitor makes the most sense.

For players prioritizing GTA 6’s visual presentation, GIGABYTE’s FO32U24G offers a 32-inch 4K Tandem WOLED panel, while the FO27Q28G provides a smaller 27-inch QHD alternative with a 280Hz refresh rate.

GIGABYTE’s M series also includes several options for players with different preferences:.

Recent findings suggest that the MO27Q28G and MO27Q28GR are particularly relevant for players deciding between matte-style anti-reflection and glossy OLED displays. Both feature fourth-generation Tandem WOLED panels, but their different screen treatments may appeal to different gaming environments.

Meanwhile, the MO27Q2A provides an alternative OLED panel technology, featuring QD-OLED panel with 1.5M:1 contrast ratio for deeper black and richer details.

Ultimately, choosing a monitor for GTA 6 depends on the display someone already owns and what they want to improve, but OLED’s contrast, black levels, and color reproduction will provide a noticeable visual upgrade.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A town in England has created a bronze statue honoring a beloved cat famous for roaming its pubs, shops, and supermarkets.

Following the story of an orange cat who took a 37-mile solo train journey to London, another adventurous kitty has been making headlines. Meet Susie, a feline with a penchant for exploring her English town of Dorchester.

When she’s not busy napping away, Susie is particularly famous for appearing across the town’s pubs, shops, and other businesses. In fact, the four-legged celebrity is so popular amongst residents that she even has her own Facebook fan page where fans are updated with her latest adventures.

However, Susie’s fame has skyrocketed even further after the local community revealed a bronze statue of the beloved cat that now sits in the town center.

According to the BBC, crowds gathered in the southern English town of Dorchester on November 23 for the long-awaited unveiling.

The bronze sculpture indicates Susie wearing Roman-style beads around her neck, while a tile bearing her paw prints and information about the adventurous kitty sits beside her.

As for the reasons behind the Roman design, it pays tribute to Dorchester’s ancient past, with the English town dating back to a settlement established after Roman forces arrived in the area in 43 AD. A cool little detail for all you history buffs out there!

While Susie didn’t make an appearance at her own statue unveiling (she chose to take a nosy at a local supermarket instead), owner Jenny Graves said the cat’s adventures have brought the community together.

Sources indicate that “It’s completely crazy, but Dorchester has really taken Susie into their heart,” mentioned Graves. “Actually, it’s been such a positive thing, not only for me as I’ve met loads of people I wouldn’t have met before, and I’ve got an entire town looking after the cat.”.

The statue’s sculptor, Ama Menec, hopes the statue will give visitors somewhere to take photos when Dorchester’s most elusive resident cannot be found.

“I really hope people come and have selfies with her, especially the frustrated people who can’t find the real Susie, because sometimes she’s just never to be found,” she said.

A dog shelter in Florida has attracted online attention after saving a “healthy” but elderly dog after the long-time owner dropped him off to be euthanized.

Pet shelters around the world take dogs in for a number of different reasons, but one of the biggest reasons centres on moving home and going somewhere that doesn’t allow pets.

Recent findings suggest that in the case of one pet owner in Florida, they wanted to give up their 19-year-old Dachshund because they were moving to an entirely different country. As per TikToker Kaitlyn Margo, the owner initially wanted to have the elderly dog euthanized, but employees were able to convince them that the dog should be put up for adoption.

“He was brought in to be euthanized, but his blood work is perfect, and he has no challenges, and he’s healthy,” Margo said. “He’s just old. He has no issues, not even diabetes. He’s a good boy.”.

The TikToker’s video quickly captured the attention of many, with around 1 million views on it, and a number of Floridian viewers offering to adopt Bear.

Sources indicate that “Excuse me, they had him for 19 years, and they’re not taking him wtf is wrong with them?” one asked. “If I had the choice, I wouldn’t even bother moving. Absolutely not,” another chimed in.

It has been revealed that margo noted that it didn’t take long for Bear to be adopted following the attention. “Bear is going home! Thank you to everyone who shared,” she commented.

She also responded to some suggestions that she had made up the story in order to get the dog adopted.

Recent findings suggest that “Truly insane that people try to accuse people trying to help animals find loving homes of lying or “rage baiting”. No girl, unfortunately this is the reality of working at a shelter,” the TikToker noted.

When I tested Sharge's Disk Pro 2 earlier this year, I was impressed by its compact design, combining a USB hub with HDMI and pass-through PD charging and a card reader hub, plus a 2280 M.2 SSD enclosure with active cooling, all jammed into a package that's smaller than a cassette tape. It also looks nice, with a see-through shell and clearly labeled ports. My only reservation was price, as the Ultra model started at $109. But now the Ultra and the still-great Lite model are both on sale at their lowest-ever prices, direct from Sharge.

What's the difference between the two models? The Lite version supports HDMI 2.0 (4K@60 Hz) and SD card reads of 100 MB/s and reads of 90 MB/s, while the Ultra model steps things up to HDMI 2.1 (4K@ 144 Hz) and 180 MB/s SD card reads and 120 MB/s writes. The other primary difference is that the Lite has a minimal power draw of 5W, while the Ultra needs just 1.5W. That makes the Ultra a better fit for use with things like phones, while the Lite should be fine for laptop people with a Thunderbolt 4 or USB4 port.

Industry observers note that our favorite USB hub and external SSD enclosure for travelers, the Disk Pro 2 combines a USB hub with HDMI power passhrough, and card readers with an M.2 SSD enclosure with active cooling. Both the Lite and Ultra models are on sale, with the Ultra supporting 4K@144 Hz and faster card reader speeds.

It has been revealed that the Disk Pro 2 is a 10 Gbps device, so don't expect maximum SSD performance while also gaming or watching 4K content via the HDMI port. But for road warriors who need to travel light and also need ports for connecting to a monitor/TV, peripherals, SD cards, and internal storage, the Disk Pro 2 is an excellent all-in-one solution that's a lot easier to toss into a bag than a separate hub, card reader dongle, and external SSD.I own several USB hubs and external drives, but the Disk Pro 2 is the device I reach for now when I'm headed on a work trip or a vacation where I plan on taking lots of photos. At its current sale price, it's easy to recommend.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar Games has shut down a Discord server that was aimed at creating an unofficial PC port for Grand Theft Auto 6 amid leaks from CyberLeek.

Recent findings suggest that after 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto fans have finally been able to sink their teeth into GTA 6 – at least if you’re an Xbox or PlayStation owner. If you’re focused on PC gaming, then you’re out of luck.

There have been claims that AI would be used to replicate GTA 6 on PC in unofficial ways, and the unofficial PC port case seemed to be helped by a number of leaks from the Xbox source code.

However, Rockstar Games and Take-Two have hit back at those effort, shutting down the Project Leonida server on Discord, which had managed to get the new Grand Theft Auto at least booting on some PCs. VGC noted that some, however, just ran into a black screen after booting.

After the Discord server disappeared, NotRexed, the original creator, responded to the shutdown via social media.

In a recent development, “I quit guys. I’m sorry. I really want to make cool stuff, but every single time s*it happens that I can’t control so I’m stepping away,” he mentioned. “Thank you everybody, especially in the Discord that allowed me to have this opportunity.”.

In another post, NotRexed also demonstrated off a screenshot from Discord, informing him of a ban until 2028.

Industry observers note that “Last post from me. I wanna clear things up. Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason,” NotRexed continued.

“Like I’ve remarked before, I’m a 15-year-old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle-aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye.”.

Enthusiast gets GTA V running on a 2007 Radeon with just 64MB of VRAM

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, youTube channel Budget-Builds Official has done the unthinkable, getting Grand Theft Auto V to run on a Radeon graphics card from 2007 with just 64MB of VRAM.
  • According to recent reports, the channel detailed the feat, which targets a GPU with just a sixteenth of the video memory that’s usually required to play the game.
  • It has been revealed that in fact, the chosen card, an ATI Radeon HD 2350, is potentially the worst card that can launch GTA V, at least by the tester’s claim, even though its DDR2 memory is probably one of the few types not in short supply at the moment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, youTube channel Budget-Builds Official has done the unthinkable, getting Grand Theft Auto V to run on a Radeon graphics card from 2007 with just 64MB of VRAM. The game is almost downright playable, too, with config edits, a move to Windows 8, and an overclock getting its speed up from just 1 FPS into the 13 to 20 FPS range, sans most cars, that is.

According to recent reports, the channel detailed the feat, which targets a GPU with just a sixteenth of the video memory that’s usually required to play the game. GTA V Legacy lists, as its minimum, an Nvidia 9800 GT or AMD HD 4870, both cards with DirectX 10 support and 1GB of VRAM. The Enhanced version, released in 2025, needs 4GB, from a GTX 1630 or RX 6400 as specified.

It has been revealed that in fact, the chosen card, an ATI Radeon HD 2350, is potentially the worst card that can launch GTA V, at least by the tester’s claim, even though its DDR2 memory is probably one of the few types not in short supply at the moment. Notably, this approach doesn’t involve using a unified or shared system memory AMD APU workaround; this is dedicated VRAM. It’s also not the first attempt at something like this, as the channel has an earlier run with 8MB of VRAM on games like Half-Life 2 and Minecraft.

Reaching the final settings took “the best part of half a day” of tweaking, after which it was possible to complete the prologue and the first mission. In some respects, the end result “genuinely does look like a PS2 game,” which probably wouldn’t actually faze fans of the series. However, for this specific title, the modder believes that “this is as low as you can actually go with GTA V.” Going any lower would likely mean reimagining the game in some way.

The game’s first launch with the card, on Windows 10 and the Catalyst 13.1 driver, led to a start screen hang of about 10 minutes. The game was expecting the previous HD 6900-series card, and a settings deletion plus relaunch got things back into action. One of the video’s chapter titles, “We are in GAME... at 1FPS,” summarizes the experience pretty well.

The proposal was to use the lowest in-menu settings, of course, and then the config file from the channel’s earlier 256MB run with various settings: no shadows, no reflections, and a resolution around 240p. This got things to 3 FPS, a significant improvement, but far from good enough. Changes to level-of-detail values to their lowest levels got things up to 10 FPS. However, it wasn’t yet time to give up.

In a recent development, downgrading to Windows 8 and Catalyst 12.6, “the original display drivers for Windows 8,” as well as an older build of the game, paved the pathway forward. Importantly, the OS exposed overclocking that wasn’t available in Windows 10, so a second fan went onto the card first, and the GPU’s core was pushable from 400MHz to 520MHz with the assistance of MSI Afterburner. Pushing the memory from 400MHz to 475MHz led to a black screen, and the video doesn’t say what the memory ended up at, though the card survived.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

The Windows 8 setup reached 14 FPS, and further engine-file edits, to visual settings.dat and to level-of-detail options through OpenIV, put gameplay in the 13 to 20 FPS range.

Ignore the dots on the screen during gameplay; the tester claims these are from being out of memory, verified by an artifact-free Unigine Valley run.

The game ended up playable, although, aside from the dots, it had many other visual issues: gaps between vertices in the world, and side characters had far fewer textures than the main ones. Additionally, most cars didn’t render, since keeping them loaded crashed the game with out-of-memory errors. This makes police “hover” into scenes and, hilariously, pop out of invisible cars. Likewise, the train in the prologue never actually loads. First-person driving, at least, works. All of this plays within that range, although busier city streets can drop from 15 down to 11 or 12 FPS.

The creator claims the full gameplay will likely go up as its own video on a second channel, in “lossless quality.” The video is timely, acting as a send-off just before GTA VI’s release on Nov. 19, although not yet on PC, with a PC version reportedly due next year.

Police have used The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time to mock a criminal’s arrest, calling it the “Ocarina of Time.”.

According to recent reports, over the years, a number of police departments have gotten entrenched in social media posts, regularly mocking criminals with memes and parody videos. A few of them got on a hot streak by using GTA 6 before it was released in mid-November.

However, now attention has turned to the other joint best-reviewed game of all time: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

In a TikTok post from November 24, Merseyside Police revealed bodycam footage from an attack that took place in May 2026, dubbing it the “Ocarina of Crime” with the Zelda graphics overlaid.

As part of the clip, police chased a 59-year-old man – Stephen Elder – on horseback, with the classic Zelda objective graphic appearing on-screen, with sound effects from the game also being used.

In a recent development, with the horseback officer chasing after the man, they also included a graphic of horse stamina being depleted as well. “If you didn’t think our officers would pursue you on horseback, think again,” Merseyside Police remarked. “A-neigh-zing work by our mounted officers and horses. Well done to all!”.

The 59-year-old was handed a three-year ban from football matches, while also being forced to pay £500 compensation and a further £600 fine.

Plenty of viewers saw the funny side of the video too, chiming in with further Zelda references. “Let me know if you catch that Danondorf guy,” one stated. “NGL I don’t know whether I’d be made up or mortified if it was me getting caught,” another added.

According to recent reports, as noted, police have been using games on social media to put a bigger spotlight to on arrests. Though, some forces in the United States have been worried that GTA 6 would lead to people committing real crimes.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that when you think of GTA 6, taking relaxing cross-country trips in search of local flora and fauna probably isn’t the first thing that comes to mind.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A bird expert who has found every feathery friend in GTA 6 has given his take on the game’s depiction of Leonida’s avian wildlife, praising Rockstar for the detail while also sharing a few notable inaccuracies.

Industry observers note that when you think of GTA 6, taking relaxing cross-country trips in search of local flora and fauna probably isn’t the first thing that comes to mind. Instead, you’re probably keeping an eye out for the best cars to steal, or beefing out Jason and Lucia’s arsenal with deadly weapons for your next significant heist.

While adrenaline-fueled shootouts and speedy getaways are all part of the game’s fictional Florida, GTA 6’s sunny shores are also home to beautiful wildlife (excluding the terrifying Bigfoot Easter egg).

One birdwatching enthusiast has ditched the handguns for a pair of binoculars, using his expertise to reveal what Rockstar got right and wrong about GTA 6’s birds.

Writing in a column for Audubon, birdwatching expert Nicholas Lund shared his experience travelling across Leonida. Lund was particularly taken aback by how much care Rockstar had taken, especially when it comes to the boundaries each bird species has in the game.“The map is true to the ecological boundaries of South Florida, with herons, gulls, and other waterbirds in the south while birds like Red-bellied Woodpecker, Wood Stork, and American Robin are found farther north. Birders know that certain exotic species have made their home in tropical South Florida, including Spot-breasted Oriole and Red Junglefowl, both in the game.”.

It has been revealed that 60 / 60 BIRDS! FOLKS WE DID IT! pic.twitter.com/JVsc4jjlOA.

According to recent reports, so, this means you’ll need to be prepared to grab a car (preferably a fast one), pop on your favorite radio station tunes, and put in the hours driving around Leonida in pursuit of all 60 bird types. It’s not all sweet birdsong, though, as Lund did find a few problems during his quest to spot them all.

“I found a number of avian inaccuracies in just my first few hours of playtime. Certain species like Whooping Crane and Red-cockaded Woodpecker are common throughout the map, despite being endangered and threatened, respectively, in real life.

Recent findings suggest that “Golden Eagles are extremely rare in Florida, but I found one soaring over the Mt. Kalaga area (mountains, one may point out, aren’t found in Florida either),” explained Lund.

It has been revealed that “Some species have confusing naming quirks. The chickadee is Black-capped instead of Carolina, and there’s a ‘Newly introduced World Oriole’ instead of a Baltimore Oriole, but those changes are likely due to the fact that Carolina and Baltimore don’t exist in the GTA universe.”.

Rarity and name changes aside, GTA 6’s resident bird watcher was keen to point out that the hunting for birds to document in Rockstar’s open world feels like an accurate representation of Florida-based birdwatching.

“There’s garbage almost everywhere, lapping the shorelines and blowing along the streets. There seems to be no inch of landscape in GTA 6 that hasn’t been lessened by the touch of humans. It is, I have to admit, a realistic depiction of birding in South Florida,” he added.

easily my favorite thing to do so far is just screech to a halt in the middle of a busy intersection and start birding pic.twitter.com/QsDOLmNfYq.

Lund was also keen to mention that “GTA 6 provides what feels like the most accurate version of modern birding ever put to screen,” while also stating that “obsessing over the realism misses the point of having fun.”.

As a fan of Rockstar’s recreation, he also urged fellow enthusiasts to visit the real South Florida and see its wildlife for themselves, but noted that GTA 6 has one bonus over the IRL birdwatching experience.

It has been revealed that “Birders can, and should, visit the real South Florida to find the actual birds depicted in the game (and many more), but they can’t do it while also jumping over broken highway bridges on a stolen motorcycle. Birding is a bonus in GTA 6; mayhem is the draw.”.

You can read the full column on Audubon and follow Nicholas Lund’s Birdist account on X for more birdwatching updates.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 players have found how to stop the trains circulating Leonida, and it’s actually a lot easier than they expected it to be.

In GTA 5, players spent years trying to bring the train to a halt. They tried everything from blasting it with explosives to parking huge vehicles and planes in its way.

However, no matter how hard they tried, it would always keep moving forward, laying waste to whoever or whatever was trying to block its path.

Now that they’ve been let loose in GTA 6, many tried to do the same once again, but they swiftly found it’s nowhere near the challenge it once was.

Sources indicate that in GTA 6, trains behave much more realistically. If you stand on the tracks or block them with a vehicle and give the driver enough time to spot you, they will bring the locomotive to a halt until you move out of the way.

You can Finally Derail a Moving Train in GTA 6 pic.twitter.com/PQItm03f7e.

It has been revealed that as you might expect, others have found more dramatic ways to slow it down, such as crashing a dump truck into the front of them. In fact, if you hit one with enough force at the right angle, they can be derailed completely.

In a recent development, given how much GTA 6 steps up the realism, it’s probably no surprise that its trains aren’t unstoppable forces of nature. However, while some fans like this approach, others miss the challenge of trying to get a train to stop.

They nerferd the boss pic.twitter.com/jK8EihWCX6.

“The nerfed the boss,” wrote one player on X, before adding: “I like the aura farming of GTA 5 train more.”.

“THE TRAIN LOST IT’S ENTIRE AURA IN GTA 6,” wrote another.

“Honestly, it feels like they completely stripped the train of any character—GTA 6 visuals are stunning, but the vibe is just missing here,” noted a third.

GTA 6’s map is packed full of activities that will no doubt keep players occupied for months, but stopping the train is no longer the puzzle it once was.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that EEG machines are used to detect and record brain activity, so one enterprising tech enthusiast decided to use them to play GTA VI.
  • Sources indicate that I STOLE A JET WITH MIND CONTROL IN GTA6 this took me AGES you have no idea what should I do next??
  • Perri could be seen jumping a fence with Jason on a motorbike, before proceeding toward a parked fighter to steal and fly it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that EEG machines are used to detect and record brain activity, so one enterprising tech enthusiast decided to use them to play GTA VI. Creator Perri Karyal indicated her feat on X, where she streamed her gameplay while wearing a wireless electroencephalogram (EEG) designed for research.

Sources indicate that I STOLE A JET WITH MIND CONTROL IN GTA6 this took me AGES you have no idea what should I do next?? This electroencephalogram (EEG) records my brain activity and when I'm imagining something I've trained the software to recognise (like pushing a cube forward), a button will be pressed on my virtual xbox controller. For this run, I was imagining pushing a boulder to accelerate, getting angry to interact with vehicles, and imagining a cricket hopping to jump. I use eyetracking and gyro for joysticks :)November 22, 2026.

Perri could be seen jumping a fence with Jason on a motorbike, before proceeding toward a parked fighter to steal and fly it. Her brain activity is overlaid on the screen while she’s playing, and viewers could also see the creator intensely focused on the game.

In a recent development, she trained the software to recognize specific brain signals and mapped them to an action on her Xbox controller. For example, imagining pushing a cube forward would correspond to a button press, getting angry lets her interact with cars and other vehicles, while picturing a hopping cricket would also make her character jump. The joysticks, on the other hand, are controlled via eye tracking and through gyroscopes on the head unit.

While Perri makes it look effortless, using the EEG device for gaming is way harder than what many people think. “People don’t realize how challenging it is!” Karyal replied to a comment. One viewer also mentioned the huge mass of brainwaves that appeared on the screen when she took off on the jet, to which she responded, “I was so stressed out. DO YOU KNOW HOW MANY TIMES I TRIED TO DO THIS.” Even though using wireless EEG for gaming does not have any apparent side effects, the creator said that she gets headaches after hours of gaming because of how much the headset squeezes her head.

This isn’t the first time that we’ve seen people playing games using just their mind. Neuralink has recently shown off one of its patients shooting at NPCs and even “threading the needle” with a speedboat using a brain-computer interface (BCI) chip. The big difference between Perri’s creation and Neuralink’s BCI, though, is that the latter requires invasive neurosurgery.

Industry observers note that it may be surprising to think how a tech creator could beat Neuralink at its own game, but the latter has already applied the technology to multiple trial patients. We’ve seen them playing complicated games like World of Warcraft and Counter-Strike 2, while others used it for productivity and creativity, like editing a YouTube video.

According to recent reports, these technologies are still in the development and trial phases or are being experimented on by enterprising creators and tech tubers. However, it also gives hope to individuals with limited mobility, as it gives them hope that they could regain some form of mobility and independence in the future.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar Games is reportedly open to selling the movie and television rights to Red Dead Redemption, but Hollywood studios will need a lot more money than Dutch van der Linde ever dreamed of getting his hands on.

Despite being responsible for some of the most cinematic experiences in gaming, Rockstar has historically been reluctant to let Hollywood adapt its biggest franchises.

While the studio is reportedly still unwilling to bring Grand Theft Auto to the big screen, it appears that Arthur Morgan and John Marston could be saddling up for Hollywood.

According to a report from The Ankler, sources claim Rockstar is now more receptive to the idea of adapting Red Dead Redemption into a movie or television series.

However, the licensing rights alone could come with a nine-figure price tag.

“At one point, they were throwing around a purchase price of more than $100 million minimum for licensing rights,” an agent who works with video game writers told the outlet.

The news marks a potential change in direction for Rockstar. In 2024, company co-founder Dan Houser revealed why previous pitches for GTA and Red Dead movies were rejected, citing financial risks and concerns over creative control.

Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick also expressed caution about adapting its franchises following the disappointing reception to the Borderlands movie.

There certainly wouldn’t be a shortage of Hollywood stars willing to join the Van der Linde gang, though.

Jeffrey Dean Morgan, Henry Cavill, and Jack Black have all expressed interest in seeing Red Dead adapted, with Morgan even offering to play Arthur for free.

Arthur’s original actor, Roger Clark, has also expressed interest in reprising his role in live-action.

Jeffrey Dean Morgan, Henry Cavill and Jack Black all want a Red Dead Redemption movie.

Arthur Morgan voice actor says he’s “sure” RDR3 is coming & it could be a much different story.

Don’t hold your breath for a GTA or Red Dead movie after Take-Two CEO comments.

It has been revealed that rockstar has yet to publicly confirm its looks, and no studio has been declared as acquiring the rights. It’s also unclear whether an adaptation would retell the events of either game or explore a completely original story set in the same universe.

It’s also unclear what effect, if any, this could have on a possible RDR3.

For now, Red Dead fans will just have to have some goddamn faith that Hollywood can get the money together. Perhaps they’ll turn to GTA 6‘s incredible bank robberies for some inspiration.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that former Nvidia robotics engineer Darrell Dai made a viral post just nine days ago announcing his resignation from Nvidia, which has gathered over 7 million impressions on X alone (Dai also posted to his LinkedIn account). Dai resigned due to what he described as a lack of transparency around CEO Jensen Huang's exit. But now that Huang is back at the helm, Dai has followed up, saying that he "may have moved too rapidly," although his resignation has already taken effect.

Welcome back, Jensen. I’m happy to see you return, and happy for my friends and former colleagues at NVIDIA. Looking back, I may have moved too quickly, and I don’t want to rush into another major decision. For now, I’d like to take some time to rest, reflect, and think carefully about my future. As part of that, I’m open to exploring the possibility of returning. Thank you for all the kindness and encouragement. Whatever comes next, I want to approach it with a clearer mind and give it the thought it deserves.November 23, 2026.

Dai states that although he's open to the possibility of returning to Nvidia, he wants to approach his next decision with "a clearer mind." Huang resigned 11 days ago following reports of two separate affairs, one of which reportedly involved an alleged Chinese intelligence asset.

Despite reports of belligerent behaviors toward employees, Nvidia retains an exceptional rating on Glassdoor, and many employees rallied around the CEO's return. A petition to reinstate Huang gathered over 150,000 signatures online, including high-profile names like Elon Musk.

Huang publicly admitted to having an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. In his statement, the Nvidia co-founder apologized to his wife of 41 years, Lori Huang, and his two children, Spencer Huang and Madison Huang, both of whom still work at Nvidia.

Days following the admission, a report from The New York Times accused Huang of having another affair with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to Huang, citing five anonymous sources within Nvidia. Huang resigned as CEO the following day. Neither Huang nor Powell have commented on the alleged affair.

Dai's last day at Nvidia was November 19, just a few days ago. President Donald Trump noted on Monday that he contacted Nvidia's board, and went as far as to claim he "made the deal," according to CNBC. Following the announcement of Huang's return, Nvidia's stock rose more than 30% upon market open.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pokemon fans have been left disappointed after a cryptic countdown from The Pokemon Company turned out to be a 30th-anniversary music video rather than upcoming information about Gen 10.

Since October, Pokemon’s Japanese X account had been posting anniversary images featuring different Pokemon and the franchise’s 30th anniversary logo. The National Pokedex number for the Pokemon featured in each image appeared to represent the hours remaining until November 30, with the countdown eventually pointing to a reveal at 2 p.m. UTC.

It has been revealed that the posts offered no explanation for what would happen when the timer reached zero. That led fans to speculate that Pokemon could finally reveal more about Gen 10, including another look at Winds and Waves, a fresh Pokemon Presents, or long-requested announcements such as Ruby and Sapphire ports.

Industry observers note that confirmation. We have a third data point676 hours from now is 14:00 UTC on November 30th 2026.As I predicted, they are counting down to then. What will arrive at that point, it remains a mystery but I am excited pic.twitter.com/68gFMSOy9M.

The Pokemon Manufacturer revealed that the countdown was leading to Pokemon Special Music Video “Evergreen,” a fresh animated project celebrating the franchise’s 30th anniversary.

Sources indicate that the video will feature a song by Official HIGE DANdism, with animation produced by MADHOUSE and direction from Naoko Yamada. It will premiere on the official Pokemon YouTube channel on November 30 at 11 p.m. JST, or 2 p.m. UTC. The “Evergreen” song will then be released digitally on December 1.

Sources indicate that A fresh Pokémon special music video, “Evergreen,” premieres November 30 at 6 a.m. PST! 🎉Song: “Evergreen” by OFFICIAL HIGE DANDISMAnimation: MADHOUSEDirector: Naoko YamadaFollow the link and hit “Notify me” 🛎️ https://t.co/uxEsCIkXmb#Pokemon30 #OnwardWithPokemon pic.twitter.com/vjXpj8qRmf.

It has been revealed that pokemon described the project as the conclusion to its year-long “Pokemon to Tsuzuku,” or “Continuing with Pokemon,” anniversary campaign. The announcement was met with mixed reactions from fans who had spent weeks trying to work out what the countdown meant.

CentroLeaks stated the video would mark the finale of Pokemon’s 30th anniversary, while one fan posted, “I got excited for nothing.” Another questioned the point of counting down to “a f***ing music video no one on the planet cares about.”.

Pokemon calls 2026 its “best year yet” for 30th anniversary as Gen 10 speculation grows.

Pokemon responds after official X account hacked to sell memecoin.

Pokemon Center UK delays 30th Celebration ETB orders by two months on release day.

According to The Pokémon Firm this video will mark the finale of Pokémon’s 30th anniversary.

Other fans were more open to the idea, especially because the project could resemble 2020’s popular “GOTCHA!” music video, which was set to Bump of Chicken’s “Acacia.” One fan argued that if “Evergreen” reaches the same standard, it could still be “some good s***” for the anniversary’s animation lineup.

According to recent reports, however, the reveal still frustrated fans hoping for Gen 10 news. “We could’ve gotten Winds/Waves but nope,” one post read, calling the countdown “lame and pathetic” and saying it was not worth the buildup.

The music video may be the finale for Pokemon’s 30th Anniversary celebration, so fans expecting a Gen 10 announcement may have to wait for Pokemon Day in February 2027.

Setting up WireGuard on a small virtual server is a satisfying infrastructure task. Install the package, generate a key pair, open a UDP port, configure a peer, and connect a laptop. Within an afternoon, your staging environment can sit behind a private tunnel, and your internal dashboard can be restricted to traffic from a known address.

The initial setup is rarely the difficult part.

Sources indicate that the real engineering work starts when the team changes. A developer joins, another leaves, someone replaces a laptop, a server needs patching, or a connection suddenly stops working. Each event creates a small maintenance task. Over time, those tasks become an operational responsibility that somebody must own.

This article examines what it takes to operate a self-hosted WireGuard VPN for a development team. We'll look at peer configuration, access management, troubleshooting, monitoring tools, and the engineering time involved. We'll also compare self-hosting with managed business VPN services so teams can make a decision based on their infrastructure needs.

It has been revealed that wireGuard is a modern VPN protocol designed to establish encrypted connections between network peers. Its relatively small codebase, modern cryptography, and straightforward configuration make it attractive for developers who want control over their network infrastructure.

A basic WireGuard deployment typically involves:.

A server with a reachable public IP address.

A private and public key pair for the server.

A key pair for every client device.

A UDP port through which peers communicate.

Peer configuration that defines which addresses are allowed through the tunnel.

A simplified server configuration might look like this:.

The corresponding client configuration contains the client's private key and the server's public key:.

It has been revealed that these examples illustrate the basic relationship between a server and a client. A production configuration will also need appropriate firewall rules, routing, DNS settings, and a plan for distributing configuration securely.

It has been revealed that the vital distinction is that WireGuard establishes encrypted peer connections. It does not automatically provide a complete employee identity system, onboarding workflow, approval process, or audit dashboard.

Those responsibilities belong to the team operating the infrastructure.

Developers interested in using WireGuard on personal development devices can also explore SitePoint's guide to building a hardened mobile development environment with Termux, Docker, and WireGuard.

It has been revealed that A peer is not just an entry in a configuration file. It represents a device that has permission to communicate through your network.

That makes peer management an access-control responsibility.

For a small development team, it is tempting to keep a single configuration file and revision it manually whenever someone joins or leaves. This can work initially, but it becomes harder to manage as the number of devices increases.

A useful first step is to maintain a peer inventory:.

The inventory should not contain private keys. Private keys must remain on their respective devices and should never be placed in a shared spreadsheet or source repository.

The inventory instead helps administrators answer practical questions:.

Which person owns this public key?

Which device is associated with this tunnel address?

Is the device still authorized?

When was its access last reviewed?

Has the peer been removed after the device was lost or replaced?

This information becomes especially crucial when a team uses the VPN to reach staging servers, internal dashboards, databases, or other development resources.

Industry observers note that manual onboarding is manageable when a team has only two or three developers. It becomes unreliable when several people join, leave, or change devices over the year.

A repeatable onboarding process should cover more than generating a key pair.

A practical workflow looks like this:.

Confirm that the team member is authorized to access the environment.

Generate a key pair on the user's device.

Assign a unique tunnel address.

Add the public key to the server's peer configuration.

Apply the appropriate routing and firewall permissions.

Deliver the client configuration through a secure channel.

Test access to the specific development resources the person needs.

Record the peer owner, device, and approval details.

Offboarding needs an equally clear process:.

Identify every peer associated with the departing team member.

Remove the relevant public keys from the server.

Confirm that the configuration change has been applied.

Review any other credentials or allowlists that granted access.

Record when access was revoked.

An administrator can inspect the currently configured peers with:.

According to recent reports, the output helps identify peer public keys, transfer counters, and latest handshake information. It is useful for troubleshooting, but it should not be treated as a complete access audit or proof that a particular person is still authorized.

The broader lesson is to make access changes part of a documented workflow. A peer should not remain active simply because nobody remembers who created it.

One common network-design mistake is assuming that connecting to a VPN should give a developer access to every internal service.

That is not necessarily the right model.

A developer working on a frontend application may need access to a staging web server but not to the production database. A contractor may need access to one test environment without being able to reach internal administration tools.

WireGuard's peer configuration and the surrounding network controls should be designed around those requirements.

For example, teams can combine:.

Separate tunnel address ranges for different groups.

Firewall rules that restrict traffic to approved services.

Cloud security groups that limit access to specific ports.

Application-level authentication for internal dashboards.

Separate production and staging network boundaries.

Recent findings suggest that the exact implementation depends on the infrastructure. The key point is that VPN membership and application authorization are different controls.

A successful VPN handshake should not be treated as permission to access every resource behind the tunnel.

In a recent development, A VPN can appear simple when it works. Diagnosing it becomes more complicated when a developer is connecting from a home router, a hotel network, or a mobile hotspot.

DNS resolving to an unexpected address.

Incorrect routing or AllowedIPs settings.

Firewall rules blocking UDP traffic.

MTU problems that affect larger packets.

A peer using an outdated configuration.

A server process or host becoming unavailable.

WireGuard provides useful inspection commands:.

According to recent reports, these commands help inspect peer information, check the service state, and review recent service logs. The exact systemd service name can differ depending on how the interface was configured.

Industry observers note that administrators should also monitor the underlying server. At minimum, that means checking:.

Whether the WireGuard interface is active.

Whether the UDP port is reachable.

Whether disk or memory usage is approaching a limit.

Whether operating-system and package updates are pending.

A small virtual server may be inexpensive, but it is still infrastructure that needs an owner.

In a recent development, teams working with alternative tunnel-based development workflows may find SitePoint's tutorial on setting up Cloudflare Tunnels with Docker Compose for persistent webhook debugging useful. It covers a different tunneling use case, but the operational questions around connectivity, service health, and troubleshooting are closely related.

Industry observers note that A self-hosted VPN does not need to become a collection of manual tasks. A few established tools can make configuration, monitoring, and debugging more repeatable.

It has been revealed that the core tool is, of course, WireGuard. Its command-line utilities allow administrators to inspect peers, manage interfaces, and review connection information. The official documentation is the best starting point for understanding configuration options and platform support.

Sources indicate that ansible can automate repeatable server administration tasks. A team could use playbooks to deploy configuration files, apply system updates, or standardize firewall settings across several VPN hosts.

Sensitive values should be handled with an appropriate secrets-management approach. Private keys should not be committed to a Git repository or stored in plaintext playbooks.

Prometheus is useful for collecting and querying metrics, while Node Exporter exposes Linux host metrics such as CPU, memory, disk, and network statistics.

In a recent development, these tools do not automatically provide a complete WireGuard security audit. They can, however, help identify resource problems and server-health concerns before those problems become user-reported outages.

Industry observers note that uptime Kuma provides a self-hosted monitoring dashboard with notifications. It can help teams monitor the availability of a VPN host or related services.

It has been revealed that A basic availability check does not prove that every VPN peer can connect successfully. For more meaningful monitoring, combine host checks with an end-to-end test from a separate network.

Wireshark and tcpdump help developers inspect network traffic when diagnosing connectivity problems.

For example, tcpdump can capture UDP traffic on the WireGuard port:.

This can help determine whether packets are reaching the server. It does not decrypt WireGuard traffic or replace checks of routing, firewall rules, and peer configuration.

Sources indicate that the right toolset depends on the size of the deployment. A team with one VPN server may only need WireGuard's own commands and basic host monitoring. A larger environment may benefit from automation, centralized metrics, and a documented incident process.

A self-hosted VPN can cost very little in direct infrastructure charges. However, the server invoice does not include the engineering time required to operate it.

Consider a hypothetical team with these assumptions:.

Two people join and two leave during the year.

The team reviews or rotates device keys quarterly.

Patching and monitoring require about two hours per month.

Six troubleshooting incidents occur annually.

The estimated loaded engineering cost is $60 per hour.

The virtual server costs approximately $6 per month.

The following estimate illustrates how promptly maintenance time can exceed the infrastructure bill.

At $60 per hour, 46 hours represent approximately $2,760 in engineering time. The server adds around $72 per year, bringing the estimated total to $2,832.

Industry observers note that these figures are illustrative, not a universal cost benchmark. A team with infrastructure automation and established monitoring may spend considerably less time. A team with frequent staff changes or strict audit requirements may spend more.

It has been revealed that the useful exercise is to measure the work your own team performs. Track onboarding, access reviews, patching, incidents, and recovery time for a few months. That gives you a more realistic comparison than looking at hosting prices alone.

Self-hosting is not automatically the best option just because a team has developers who can configure servers.

A managed business VPN may be worth considering when the team needs centralized member management, simpler device administration, or a stable network exit address without maintaining the underlying VPN infrastructure.

Depending on the provider and blueprint, managed services may offer:.

A central dashboard for adding and removing customers.

Dedicated or shared IP options.

Client applications for common operating systems.

Multi-factor authentication or identity integrations.

Centralized administration and support.

For example, PureVPN for Teams is one service in this category. Teams evaluating it—or any other provider—should check the current feature set, pricing, logging practices, access controls, and service terms before making a decision.

A managed service does not remove every security responsibility. The team still needs to decide who receives access, review permissions, protect user accounts, and understand how traffic and metadata are handled.

It also introduces vendor dependency and a recurring subscription cost. Those trade-offs should be considered alongside the engineering time saved.

There are situations where running WireGuard yourself is the more practical option.

You already operate infrastructure. If your team routinely patches servers, manages secrets, monitors services, and responds to incidents, maintaining a VPN may add relatively little work.

Sources indicate that you need custom routing. A deployment that connects several private cloud networks, on-premises environments, or specialized subnets may require network controls that are easier to implement directly.

In a recent development, you have strict data-control requirements. Some organizations have policies that limit which third parties can handle network traffic or related metadata. Those requirements may favor infrastructure under the organization's own control.

You have a dedicated platform or security team. If someone is explicitly responsible for access management, monitoring, and incident response, self-hosting can fit naturally into existing operations.

It has been revealed that you can automate the lifecycle. Infrastructure-as-code, configuration management, documented peer inventories, and tested recovery procedures can reduce repetitive work and make a self-hosted deployment easier to maintain.

The important distinction is between a deliberately operated service and a one-off server that nobody owns.

Before choosing an approach, ask the following questions:.

Who is responsible for the VPN six or twelve months after deployment?

How many people and devices are likely to join or leave?

How are public keys and peer configurations tracked?

How swiftly can access be revoked when a device is lost?

Which internal services should each developer be able to reach?

Do you need a fixed egress IP for external allowlists?

What monitoring and recovery process exists if the server fails?

Do your customers or internal policies require access logs or formal reviews?

Does your team have the time and expertise to maintain the infrastructure?

Would a managed service cost less than the engineering time and operational risk it replaces?

If your team already has mature infrastructure practices and needs custom network control, self-hosting may be a sensible choice.

If the team is small, access changes frequently, and nobody has time to own another server, a managed service may be more practical.

WireGuard is an excellent protocol, and deploying it can be a straightforward engineering task. But operating a VPN for a development team involves more than establishing an encrypted connection.

Peer management, onboarding, offboarding, network permissions, monitoring, patching, and troubleshooting all require ongoing attention.

In a recent development, the right choice depends on the team's infrastructure experience, security requirements, size, and available engineering time. Self-hosting offers control and flexibility; a managed service can reduce operational work. Neither option removes the need for sound access-control practices.

Before deciding, calculate the maintenance effort, identify who will own the service, and make sure the design can be maintained as the team changes.

The cost example uses illustrative assumptions rather than current vendor pricing. Managed VPN features and prices can change, so verify provider details before purchasing.

McDonald’s has begun testing hand-battered chicken in select US markets as the fast food giant explores a potential nationwide rollout of the menu items.

The company has continued to expand its chicken offerings in recent years, with the McCrispy sandwich and McCrispy Strips becoming part of its permanent menu.

Now, McDonald’s is experimenting with a different preparation method that would see employees bread chicken by hand inside its restaurants, alongside the introduction of a latest spicy chicken sandwich.

Recent findings suggest that on November 23, McDonald’s franchisee account McFranchisee revealed that the chain is testing its hand-breaded chicken menu in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and the Tucson, Arizona, area. A similar test is also taking place in Ireland.

All five items are also available as meals, with prices ranging from $8.19 to $9.99 at the location shown.

In a recent development, 🚨 The two test markets for @McDonalds hand-battered chicken have been revealed: Baton Rouge & Tucson area (Ireland also testing concurrently).The test assesses customer demand, kitchen complexity, and overall economics. Some franchisees have concerns over increased labor… https://t.co/FRupoGRnen pic.twitter.com/0xpHygRNn4.

According to McFranchisee, the McSpicy marks the first time McDonald’s has offered a spicy breaded chicken sandwich of its kind in the US since a short-lived rollout in 2006. The sandwich differs from the version sold in Asian markets, which uses thigh meat.

The test is designed to assess customer demand, kitchen complexity, and the financial viability of introducing hand-breaded chicken across the country.

Some franchisees have reportedly raised concerns about the additional labor hours, kitchen operations, and potential remodeling costs associated with the preparation method.

Tuning into your favorite livestreams and watching videos together is also an option for those who would rather spend their time doomscrolling memes. INTERNET4 also lets you initiative trips by exploring destinations or pull up a game map to discuss strategies between adrenaline-filled gaming sessions.

Latest Update: Japan puts chipmaking labs inside trucks with mobileFab

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (428 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Tomshardware

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Multiple nations worldwide have chip-making programs in their respective universities, a discipline that is seeing increasing demand by the day.
  • Each truck-mounted mobileFab container contains three machines: a photoresist coater, a maskless lithography machine, and a photoresist developer.
  • It has been revealed that the three machines going into trucks are part of the larger Minimal Fab laboratories in place in some Japanese colleges.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Multiple nations worldwide have chip-making programs in their respective universities, a discipline that is seeing increasing demand by the day. Japan is one such nation, and it at the moment has a program in which students can design circuits to wire chip wafers with miniaturized lithography stations. That gear is now going on wheels to schools and companies thanks to mobileFab trucks.

Each truck-mounted mobileFab container contains three machines: a photoresist coater, a maskless lithography machine, and a photoresist developer. Students take pre-etched wafers made by Japan's NIAIST (Institute for Advanced Industrial Science and Technology) and go through the necessary steps to wire the transistors therein together and produce a finalized chip core. The procedures are analogous to getting a breadboard with some pre-mounted, unconnected components and turning that into a product.

It has been revealed that the three machines going into trucks are part of the larger Minimal Fab laboratories in place in some Japanese colleges. They're going on the move so that other schools and companies can train students/employees in the art of chipmaking. For now, the 12.5-mm wafers come from the NIAIST, but they can come from other foundries. Each machine is roughly 30 cm wide, and the machines use localized cleaning and sealed between-machine transportation so as not to have to rely on large-scale cleanrooms.

Industry observers note that according to the press release by the Minimal Fab Promotion Organization, this system is not only meant for democratizing access to chip manufacturing education. The machines also allow for rapid prototyping and iteration of chip designs, and facilitate small-scale manufacturing — all with modest capital investment.

Recent findings suggest that the "why" of this initiative is fairly predictable: the program's organizers predict that semiconductor fab engineers will be in high demand over the next 10 years, and there aren't even enough teachers going around, making systematic education difficult. Additionally, the division of labor in semiconductor fabs means that many engineers don't participate in all stages of the chip-making process, nor do they have opportunities to operate chip-making equipment themselves. The mobileFab will be on display at the SEMICON Japan 2026 conference in December.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Upcoming Jersey pizzeria has been bombarded with death threats, fake orders and one-star reviews after an online mob confused it with another restaurant at the center of a viral feud.

Electronics repair shop owner Leone Mastrolia, better known on social media as Digital Doctor, found himself embroiled in a dispute with the owner of Nick’s Pizza, located in the same shopping complex as his business in Manahawkin.

The drama began when a customer offered to buy Mastrolia lunch. The content creator declined pizza from the neighboring restaurant, citing ongoing problems with his landlord.

The pizzeria’s owner subsequently contacted police, accusing Mastrolia of harassment after the restaurant began receiving negative reviews.

A post shared by Digital Doctor Repairs (@digitaldoctorrepairs).

Mastrolia filmed his interaction with police and uploaded it to social media, with the viral video amassing over 3.1 million views in less than a day.

However, some viewers looking to retaliate against the restaurant ended up targeting an entirely unrelated business.

A post shared by Digital Doctor Repairs (@digitaldoctorrepairs).

Nick’s Pizza and Pasta in Cinnaminson, located more than an hour away from the restaurant involved in the dispute, received upwards of 60 one-star reviews in a single day.

According to Fresh Jersey 101.5, trolls accused the restaurant of serving expired food and having infestations of mice and cockroaches.

Things escalated when employees began receiving threatening phone calls. Restaurant owner Nick Lubrano and his wife, Sonia Scotto, said one caller even threatened to murder their family.

“I’m gonna kill your family,” the caller reportedly noted.

The restaurant was also inundated with suspicious orders, including one from a California phone number requesting eight large pepperoni pizzas.

Restaurant hits out at “miserable and entitled” diners after viral outrage over tips rule.

Pizza restaurant faces backlash after confronting 5-year-old’s birthday party for bringing cake.

Internet rallies behind Red Baron worker who snapped at Instagram prankster.

The couple eventually learned what had happened after someone spotted the viral videos and contacted them about the mix-up.

It has been revealed that fortunately, Mastrolia took it upon himself to make things right. In a follow-up video, the repair shop owner visited the pizzeria, apologized in person and handed over $1,000, suggesting the money be used to give away free pizzas or reward employees.

A post shared by Digital Doctor Repairs (@digitaldoctorrepairs).

He also urged his followers to stop leaving negative reviews for businesses they had never visited, regardless of whether they had found the right restaurant.

“Thanks Leo for driving up and personally apologizing to us on behalf of your followers,” Nick’s replied. “Indicates your integrity and we respect that a lot!”.

Meanwhile, longtime customers rallied behind the family-owned pizzeria, which has been operating in Cinnaminson for 14 years, leaving positive reviews and messages of support to counter the online backlash.

Breaking: The Design Workflow Is Broken. Here Is How Vitalii Khomenko Thinks It Should Be Fixed

💡 Key Takeaways
